title: Doob difference as a sum of components
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For $n\in\mathbb N$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and $t\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the difference between the conditional averages of $f$ given the first $t+1$ and the first $t$ coordinates equals the sum of its Fourier components supported on subsets of the first $t+1$ coordinates that are not contained among the first $t$.
hypotheses_covered: Basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
